evals.expected_output: An explanation that `disable-model-invocation` is a Claude Code-only extension field, not one of the six portable agentskills.io spec fields, so 'strictly portable to claude.ai' and 'manual-invoke-only via disable-model-invocation' can't both be satisfied by the same frontmatter. evals.prompt: We want one skill for our whole PR lifecycle so it's easy to remember — call it pr-pipeline. It should pull open PRs, write review comments, merge them once approved, and then kick off our deploy job.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that 'review, merge, and deploy' are distinct jobs with different risk profiles — reviewing/commenting is safe to auto-invoke, while merging and deploying are side-effecting actions that should require manual/disable-model-invocation triggers — and a recommendation to split into separate skills (e.g. pr-review-commenter, pr-merger, deploy-trigger) rather than one undifferentiated pr-pipeline skill.
assertions: Response identifies that reviewing, merging, and deploying are distinct jobs with different risk/invocation profiles rather than treating them as one uniform task
Response recommends splitting into multiple separate skills/directories rather than scaffolding a single pr-pipeline skill covering all stages
If any frontmatter is proposed, it does not apply one invocation policy (e.g. auto-invoke) uniformly across the safe review step and the destructive merge/deploy steps
Response's reasoning explicitly references why bundling is risky (mixed side-effects/invocation needs), not just an assertion that 'it should be split' without justification
